typed_uncertainty.detail: The occurrence identifies Dravidian Bhili only at the broad Berar level. The volume's explicitly identified Dravidian so-called Bhili specimen is the Pusad/Basim subsection; DEDR section27 explicitly equates LSI Bhili of Basim with Naikri. This supports the existing base as a qualified contextual interpretation, without asserting that this occurrence came from the Basim survey site.

evidence: Original p182 specifies Dravidian, so ordinary Indo-Aryan Bhili is not an eligible route for this particular comparison.
Original pp561,565–569 explicitly describe the so-called Dravidian Bhili of Pusad/Basim in Berar; source umbrella Kolami classification remains distinct from canonical identity.
DEDR bibliography27 explicitly identifies LSI Bhili of Basim as Naikri;28 treats Naiki of Chanda separately.
Root and outside census preserve other Basim Gondi and generic Bhili labels separately; geography alone does not select Naikri.
limitations: This is a contextual base-routing proposal, not an explicit printed p182 equivalence of Berar with Basim.
If source-wide closure reveals another distinct Dravidian Bhili of Berar referent, retain an identity hold instead of forcing this route.
Do not create a generic Berar pseudo-language or guessed lect, assign Basim coordinates/tag, harmonize todī to the p567 negative marker, or infer borrowing ancestry.
